items.summary: Jointly optimizes a coding agent’s policy and its surrounding harness, treating prompts, tools, workflows, and model behavior as coupled components rather than improving either in isolation.

items.title: Grounding AI agents in biological reality: Building blocks for autonomous wet labs
items.summary: Google Research describes laboratory-state verification and agent-driven molecular discovery loops using physical experimental feedback. The post distinguishes computational proposals from wet-lab execution and discusses three linked technical reports.

items.title: DiscoveryRSI: Recursively Learning to Discover Valuable Hypotheses
items.summary: This paper introduces DiscoveryRSI, which builds testable hypothesis trees through multi-agent evolutionary search and improves its research workflow using contribution credit, harness replay, and rediscovery. It also introduces DFM-Bench to evaluate hypothesis quality and cumulative research progress.
items.date_evidence: The arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 16 Oct 2026”; submission history records v1 at 17:56:35 UTC.
items.relevance: Directly addresses scientific-discovery agents, hypothesis generation, recursive self-improvement, executable investigations and process-level discovery evaluation.

items.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing Agentic Causal Discovery
items.summary: Introduces Heuresis, a benchmark of anonymized simulated datasets designed to test whether agents diagnose and repair causal-discovery errors rather than exploit semantic variable names or merely select an existing algorithm.
items.date_evidence: The arXiv page says “Submitted on 16 Oct 2026”; submission history lists v1 at 2026-10-16 02:47:51 UTC.

items.title: SciΠvot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents
items.summary: SciΠvot evaluates whether research agents make sound decisions at pivotal moments, using 248 cases derived from human interventions across 26 projects. Frontier models often preferred the original agent plan over the human correction, exposing a major scientific-judgment gap.
items.date_evidence: The arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 15 Oct 2026”; submission history records v1 at 01:34:44 UTC.
items.relevance: A highly relevant evaluation resource for autonomous research agents, focusing on consequential experimental and project-level judgment rather than final-answer accuracy.

items.title: Null Controls Are Necessary but Not Sufficient: Evaluating Acceptance Guards for Scientific Discovery and Interpretability
items.summary: This work tests acceptance criteria used by automated discovery systems and shows that seemingly successful descriptive tests can admit scientifically empty explanations. It proposes evaluating null rejection, positive acceptance and independently verified consequences together.
items.date_evidence: The arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 15 Oct 2026”; submission history records v1 at 15:13:57 UTC.
items.relevance: Targets the reliability of discovery evaluation and demonstrates why candidate hypotheses need both adversarial controls and consequence-based validation.

items.title: Data World: Scaling Data Environments from Scratch
items.summary: Data World generates synthetic data environments from explicit underlying mechanisms, along with tasks and auditable rubrics. This provides scalable, verifiable training and evaluation material for agents that must discover insights across heterogeneous files.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 15 Oct 2026.”
items.relevance: Provides a discovery-training engine and benchmark in which open-ended analytical findings can be checked against known generative truth.

items.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
items.summary: Proposes evolving scientific-agent swarms through feedback-guided mutation and recombination of hypotheses and program components, allowing partial experimental results to inform later research.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source explicitly states “Submitted on 14 Oct 2026.”
items.relevance: Combines recursive self-improvement, multi-agent exploration, transferable experimental experience, and evaluation on science and machine-learning research tasks.

items.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
items.summary: The authors find that longer or parallel agent searches plateau as accumulated histories anchor subsequent exploration. Periodically clearing search state while retaining the best candidate restores exploration and improves results on programming, kernel-optimization and model-training tasks.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 14 Oct 2026.”
items.relevance: Offers a concrete memory-management mechanism for scaling open-ended discovery and shows that forgetting can be as important as additional compute.

items.title: Research@ 2026: 10 ways we are amplifying human ingenuity
items.summary: Google Research surveys new research tools, including multi-agent scientific orchestration and empirical research assistance, with examples of reproducing methods and adapting them to new scientific settings.
items.date_evidence: Publisher page explicitly dated October 14, 2026
items.relevance: Research-system integration and scientific workflow reuse.

items.title: Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs
items.summary: Trains an LLM’s action-selection reasoning with information-gain rewards so it can conduct sequential Bayesian experimental design more cheaply and generalize its information-gathering behavior to unseen categories and clinical dialogue.
items.date_evidence: The arXiv page says “Submitted on 14 Oct 2026”; submission history lists v1 at 2026-10-14 19:15:58 UTC.

items.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
items.summary: Formalizes persistent revision of prompts, memory, workflows, tools, code, and plugins while model weights remain fixed, and analyzes admission, retention, validation, and safety requirements for accepted harness changes.
items.date_evidence: The arXiv page says “Submitted on 13 Oct 2026”; submission history lists v1 at 2026-10-13 17:48:49 UTC.

items.title: Searching for What Matters: Open-Ended Discovery of Multiple Hypotheses with Agentic Data Exploration
items.summary: This paper defines a setting where an agent receives a large table and an outcome but no predefined research question. HypAgent interactively proposes, tests and refines multiple hypotheses while removing explained signal so later searches target additional mechanisms.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 13 Oct 2026.”
items.relevance: Directly studies open-world hypothesis discovery, agentic data exploration and causal validation against hidden structural causal models.

items.title: ResearchFlow-Eval: Tracing the Execution Gap in End-to-End Multi-Claim Autoresearch
items.summary: Evaluates continuous, multi-stage research workflows at both claim and stage level. Its experiments find that execution quality trails planning, repeated attempts rarely improve results, and added skills or research orchestration do not reliably close the gap.
items.date_evidence: The arXiv page reports initial submission on 2026-10-13 and revision on 2026-10-14; v1 is the original paper date.
items.relevance: Supplies process-level evaluation for autoresearch, especially iterative execution, claim completion, and evidence-backed revision.

items.title: Into the Unknown: Benchmarking AI agents on open scientific research problems
items.summary: Introduces 15 scientist-proposed open follow-up research tasks, evaluated through paper, code, and execution-log evidence. None of 135 baseline submissions passes all strict integrity, completeness, and sufficiency requirements.

items.title: Autonomous Science Bench: Evaluating AI Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
items.summary: Autonomous Science Bench supplies six budget-constrained design-build-test-learn campaigns based on published biology, chemistry and materials experiments. It evaluates agents separately on the quality of measured discoveries and their ability to rank unseen designs.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 13 Oct 2026.”
items.relevance: A direct benchmark for experimental design and closed-loop scientific agents, with separate gates for exploration success and scientific learning.

items.title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Collective Intelligence
items.summary: Sakana AI announces MASS, in which one shared model forms virtual-agent teams, searches for better workflows, selects strong executions, and distills the team’s experience back into itself. The post also emphasizes the danger of a model sharing blind spots with its own evaluator.
items.date_evidence: The first-party Sakana AI page explicitly displays “October 12, 2026.”
items.relevance: First-party lab announcement of homogeneous multi-agent self-supervision for open-ended research and recursive improvement.

items.title: HarnessTTT: Learn to Optimize Harness at Test-Time for Scientific Discovery
items.summary: HarnessTTT trains a proposer at test time to produce executable combinations of prompts, skills, tools, middleware and execution controls while leaving the discovery executor frozen. Outcome feedback improves later harness proposals under a fixed search budget.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 12 Oct 2026.”
items.relevance: Directly connects test-time learning, agent-harness optimization and reusable discovery procedures across scientific and engineering tasks.

items.title: D-World: An Explicit World-Language-Action Model with Recursive Self-Improvement under Dual Control
items.summary: D-World represents a robot's environment as an executable digital twin that agents update from physical measurements. Proposed parameter changes are accepted only when replay does not worsen measured residuals, while action selection balances task progress against revealing model errors.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 12 Oct 2026.”
items.relevance: Combines an explicit, correctable world model with causal probing, measurement-grounded revision and recursive improvement in physical discovery.

items.title: Recursive self-improvement, part 3: code that rewrites its coder, from FunSearch to AIDE²
items.summary: Ashish Kumar analyzes code-evolving research systems and argues that current recursive improvement lives mainly in editable scaffolds, search policies, memory, and tools. The post highlights transferred gains from AIDE² but also stresses evaluator gaming across systems.
items.date_evidence: Article header explicitly states 11 October 2026.
items.relevance: Useful technical commentary on harness-level RSI, transfer, verifier limits, and the safeguards needed before running autonomous improvement loops.

items.title: TagBO: LLM-Driven Task-Aware Graph Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Discovery
items.summary: TagBO extracts coarse task-aware relationships from LLM reasoning and combines them with structural descriptors inside a graph-based Bayesian-optimization representation. items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 10 Oct 2026.”
items.relevance: A concrete experimental-design method that uses language-model priors to improve sample-efficient scientific optimization.

items.title: Pre-Registered Genesis Accounting for Recursive Self-Improvement: First Audited Operator-Genesis Events in a Physics-Discovery Runtime
items.summary: This work proposes auditable accounting that distinguishes content generated with designer-supplied mechanisms from genuinely machine-authored operator types. items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 10 Oct 2026.”

items.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
items.summary: Uses predictive world models to guide action and learning-data selection, while observed feedback controls policy or workflow improvement and conditional world-model adaptation.

items.summary: OpenSocialJax varies layouts and hidden rules across tens of millions of possible social-dilemma environments. Repeated trials test whether language-model agents can discover environmental rules while adapting to teammates and maintaining cooperation.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 9 Oct 2026.”

items.summary: Adds co-evolving predictive world models to autonomous research loops so agents can forecast experiment outcomes and allocate costly executions more strategically instead of relying only on reactive trial and error.

items.title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
items.summary: Presents MASS, an RSI loop where a shared model acts as task solver, workflow optimizer, and evaluator through multiple agent instances, then trains on selected team trajectories to internalize collective improvements.

items.summary: Kernaut lets coding agents invent kernel functions as programs while construction contracts guarantee mathematical validity. items.summary: Procedurally generates synthetic biobanks with concealed but known causal structure, enabling end-to-end training and evaluation of AI scientists for causal drug-target discovery without exposing private participant data.

items.summary: Station places multiple agents in an open-world scientific ecosystem and adds supervision plus periodic meta-reflection to sustain research when intermediate metrics are absent. Agents are evaluated by how many findings from withheld research papers they independently rediscover.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 6 Oct 2026.”
items.relevance: Direct evidence about discovery-agent environments, persistent exploration, multi-agent research and evaluation through independent rediscovery.

items.title: Fork-and-Flush: Escaping Idea Basins in Autoresearch Agents
items.summary: Studies why independent autoresearch runs settle into different local idea regions and proposes branching and selective context removal to encourage broader exploration beyond an agent’s current trajectory.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source verifies the title under identifier 2610.07447 and reports the original submission date as 2026-10-05.

items.title: Evolving in Thought Space: Training a Small Model at Test Time Unlocks Better Discoveries
items.summary: Guidance-TTT adapts a compact model at test time to suggest high-level strategy changes while a stronger frozen model implements complete executable solutions. This separates strategic learning from implementation and reduces the cost of discovery-time policy updates.

items.title: From Scientific Observations to Mechanisms: Benchmarking Hypothesis Generation by AI Scientists
items.summary: Introduces MechHypoBench, which tests whether AI scientists can infer mechanisms from complex empirical observations across 14 fields and 17.98 million records. items.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 4 October 2026 at 13:10:47 UTC.

items.title: CURIO: Curiosity-Driven Test-Time Learning for Open-Ended Discovery
items.summary: CURIO augments task-reward learning with prediction-error bonuses from an intrinsic world model, encouraging exploration beyond the policy's most likely outputs. It reports gains on mathematical-discovery tasks and single-cell denoising together with increased program diversity.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 4 Oct 2026.”
items.relevance: Combines open-ended exploration, learned world-model signals and test-time reinforcement learning for scientific discovery.

items.title: Are We Measuring Scientific Intelligence? Rethinking the Evaluation of AI Scientists
items.summary: Tests whether AI-scientist answers actually follow supplied evidence by withdrawing or reversing evidence in benchmark data. High ordinary accuracy fell sharply under an evidence-grounded metric, showing that prior knowledge and shortcuts can masquerade as scientific reasoning.
items.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 4 October 2026 at 03:50:36 UTC.

items.title: When Is Enough Enough in Self-Evolving LLM Systems?
items.summary: Develops an anytime-valid detector for deciding when iterative self-evolution should stop and a change-point method for selecting an earlier artifact when late updates overfit. Reported experiments substantially reduce compute while preserving unseen-test performance.
items.date_evidence: arXiv source page submission history identifies the initial October 3, 2026 version; candidate metadata agrees.

items.title: Recursive Self-Improvement: What Happens When AI Helps Build Better AI
items.summary: A public explainer separates ordinary AI-assisted engineering, supervised task leadership, and fully autonomous successor training, while comparing recent lab claims with skeptical arguments and emphasizing unresolved measurement caveats.

items.title: EvoCast: Reliable Autonomous Research Agents for Iterative Forecasting Architecture Evolution
items.summary: Presents an autonomous forecasting-research system that diagnoses baselines, proposes evidence-grounded architecture changes, executes them, and accumulates results. items.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 3 October 2026 at 13:30:53 UTC.
items.relevance: A strong example of controlled AutoResearch combining open-ended exploration with reproducible experimental governance.

items.title: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Build Their Own Feedback for Recursive Self-Improvement?
items.summary: Benchmarks agents that design executable evaluators by selecting tasks, implementing graders, and repairing them through pilots. The best agent-built evaluators approximate target-benchmark rankings but still suffer failures such as truncation and budget exhaustion.

items.title: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses
items.summary: Allows an optimizer to revise both an executor's harness and its own prompts, skills, tools, hooks, and notes while keeping model weights frozen. Execution-based verification, replay, and regression tracking produced held-out and out-of-distribution gains.
items.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 2 October 2026 at 00:16:30 UTC.

items.title: Scientific Discovery under Validation Congestion via Multi-Fidelity Pairwise Rankings
items.summary: PRISMS prioritizes candidate molecules, materials and other designs using pairwise expert preferences instead of data-hungry absolute-score regressors. It selectively escalates uncertain comparisons to more expensive experts using a Fisher-information criterion.

items.summary: Studies runtime selection and coordination among agents drawn from existing AI-scientist systems. Runtime agent selection improved observed mean scores, while extra contracts and verification had mixed effects under constrained budgets.
items.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 1 October 2026 at 03:18:07 UTC.

items.title: SimEX: Simulation-Integrated Robotics AutoResearch
items.summary: Combines open-ended simulation experiments with a small number of physical trials to build and repair reusable robot tools. The reported system acquired manipulation skills without demonstrations and with ten minutes of real-robot interaction.

items.summary: Builds a continually growing library of decision-relevant experimental experience. An agent retrieves prior evidence and runs a low-cost pilot only when that evidence is insufficient before committing to expensive full evaluation.

items.summary: Evaluates whether repeatedly rewritten agent skills transfer beyond the tasks used to evolve them. It focuses on the gap between training-task improvement and genuine held-out generalization across several self-evolving skill methods.

items.relevance: A critical evaluation of persistent skill evolution and whether apparent self-improvement survives distribution shift.

items.summary: Shows that scalar feedback can hide tradeoffs among competing model behaviors. ConflictGuide exposes behavior-level conflicts so an AutoResearch loop can pursue edits that resolve them rather than merely improving a single aggregate score.
items.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source is record 2609.39933; its original-version metadata gives 30 September 2026.

paper_pages.date_evidence: The arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 15 Oct 2026”; submission history records v1 at 01:34:44 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: A highly relevant evaluation resource for autonomous research agents, focusing on consequential experimental and project-level judgment rather than final-answer accuracy.

paper_pages.title: Null Controls Are Necessary but Not Sufficient: Evaluating Acceptance Guards for Scientific Discovery and Interpretability
paper_pages.summary: This work tests acceptance criteria used by automated discovery systems and shows that seemingly successful descriptive tests can admit scientifically empty explanations. It proposes evaluating null rejection, positive acceptance and independently verified consequences together.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 15 Oct 2026”; submission history records v1 at 15:13:57 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: Targets the reliability of discovery evaluation and demonstrates why candidate hypotheses need both adversarial controls and consequence-based validation.

paper_pages.title: Data World: Scaling Data Environments from Scratch
paper_pages.summary: Data World generates synthetic data environments from explicit underlying mechanisms, along with tasks and auditable rubrics. This provides scalable, verifiable training and evaluation material for agents that must discover insights across heterogeneous files.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 15 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Provides a discovery-training engine and benchmark in which open-ended analytical findings can be checked against known generative truth.

paper_pages.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
paper_pages.summary: Proposes evolving scientific-agent swarms through feedback-guided mutation and recombination of hypotheses and program components, allowing partial experimental results to inform later research.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source explicitly states “Submitted on 14 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Combines recursive self-improvement, multi-agent exploration, transferable experimental experience, and evaluation on science and machine-learning research tasks.

paper_pages.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
paper_pages.summary: The authors find that longer or parallel agent searches plateau as accumulated histories anchor subsequent exploration. Periodically clearing search state while retaining the best candidate restores exploration and improves results on programming, kernel-optimization and model-training tasks.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 14 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Offers a concrete memory-management mechanism for scaling open-ended discovery and shows that forgetting can be as important as additional compute.

paper_pages.title: Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs
paper_pages.summary: Trains an LLM’s action-selection reasoning with information-gain rewards so it can conduct sequential Bayesian experimental design more cheaply and generalize its information-gathering behavior to unseen categories and clinical dialogue.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The arXiv page says “Submitted on 14 Oct 2026”; submission history lists v1 at 2026-10-14 19:15:58 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: Directly advances adaptive experiment selection, a core capability for discovery agents operating under limited evidence and budgets.

paper_pages.title: Self-Evolving Agent Harness
paper_pages.summary: Formalizes persistent revision of prompts, memory, workflows, tools, code, and plugins while model weights remain fixed, and analyzes admission, retention, validation, and safety requirements for accepted harness changes.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The arXiv page says “Submitted on 13 Oct 2026”; submission history lists v1 at 2026-10-13 17:48:49 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: A foundational treatment of harness-level recursive self-improvement, including generalization safeguards and institutional consequences.

paper_pages.title: Searching for What Matters: Open-Ended Discovery of Multiple Hypotheses with Agentic Data Exploration
paper_pages.summary: This paper defines a setting where an agent receives a large table and an outcome but no predefined research question. HypAgent interactively proposes, tests and refines multiple hypotheses while removing explained signal so later searches target additional mechanisms.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 13 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Directly studies open-world hypothesis discovery, agentic data exploration and causal validation against hidden structural causal models.

paper_pages.title: ResearchFlow-Eval: Tracing the Execution Gap in End-to-End Multi-Claim Autoresearch
paper_pages.summary: Evaluates continuous, multi-stage research workflows at both claim and stage level. Its experiments find that execution quality trails planning, repeated attempts rarely improve results, and added skills or research orchestration do not reliably close the gap.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The arXiv page reports initial submission on 2026-10-13 and revision on 2026-10-14; v1 is the original paper date.
paper_pages.relevance: Supplies process-level evaluation for autoresearch, especially iterative execution, claim completion, and evidence-backed revision.

paper_pages.title: Autonomous Science Bench: Evaluating AI Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
paper_pages.summary: Autonomous Science Bench supplies six budget-constrained design-build-test-learn campaigns based on published biology, chemistry and materials experiments. It evaluates agents separately on the quality of measured discoveries and their ability to rank unseen designs.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 13 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: A direct benchmark for experimental design and closed-loop scientific agents, with separate gates for exploration success and scientific learning.

paper_pages.title: HarnessTTT: Learn to Optimize Harness at Test-Time for Scientific Discovery
paper_pages.summary: HarnessTTT trains a proposer at test time to produce executable combinations of prompts, skills, tools, middleware and execution controls while leaving the discovery executor frozen. Outcome feedback improves later harness proposals under a fixed search budget.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 12 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Directly connects test-time learning, agent-harness optimization and reusable discovery procedures across scientific and engineering tasks.

paper_pages.title: D-World: An Explicit World-Language-Action Model with Recursive Self-Improvement under Dual Control
paper_pages.summary: D-World represents a robot's environment as an executable digital twin that agents update from physical measurements. Proposed parameter changes are accepted only when replay does not worsen measured residuals, while action selection balances task progress against revealing model errors.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 12 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Combines an explicit, correctable world model with causal probing, measurement-grounded revision and recursive improvement in physical discovery.

paper_pages.title: TagBO: LLM-Driven Task-Aware Graph Bayesian Optimization for Scientific Discovery
paper_pages.summary: TagBO extracts coarse task-aware relationships from LLM reasoning and combines them with structural descriptors inside a graph-based Bayesian-optimization representation. Experiments target mixed categorical and continuous chemistry and materials searches under limited evaluation budgets.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 10 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: A concrete experimental-design method that uses language-model priors to improve sample-efficient scientific optimization.

paper_pages.title: Pre-Registered Genesis Accounting for Recursive Self-Improvement: First Audited Operator-Genesis Events in a Physics-Discovery Runtime
paper_pages.summary: This work proposes auditable accounting that distinguishes content generated with designer-supplied mechanisms from genuinely machine-authored operator types. Its physics runtime reports held-out validation of newly composed operators while documenting protocol flaws and limits to autonomy.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 10 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Develops falsifiable evaluation and governance for recursive self-improvement claims in a scientific-discovery setting.

paper_pages.title: RSI-Anything: Unlocking Recursive Self-Improvement with World Models
paper_pages.summary: Uses predictive world models to guide action and learning-data selection, while observed feedback controls policy or workflow improvement and conditional world-model adaptation.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source verifies the title under identifier 2610.13912 and reports the original submission date as 2026-10-09.
paper_pages.relevance: Directly connects recursive self-improvement with adaptive world models and feedback-efficient discovery across domains.

paper_pages.title: OpenSocialJax: Evaluating Social Adaptation in Sequential Social Dilemmas with Open-Ended Environmental Dynamics
paper_pages.summary: OpenSocialJax varies layouts and hidden rules across tens of millions of possible social-dilemma environments. Repeated trials test whether language-model agents can discover environmental rules while adapting to teammates and maintaining cooperation.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 9 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: A useful open-world evaluation of continual inference and adaptation under unfamiliar environmental dynamics and changing multi-agent behavior.

paper_pages.title: JANUS: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models
paper_pages.summary: Adds co-evolving predictive world models to autonomous research loops so agents can forecast experiment outcomes and allocate costly executions more strategically instead of relying only on reactive trial and error.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source verifies the title under identifier 2610.13194 and reports the original submission date as 2026-10-09.
paper_pages.relevance: Targets long-horizon scientific agents, experiment planning, delayed feedback, and scalable exploration of large research spaces.

paper_pages.title: Harness^2: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World
paper_pages.summary: Harness^2 uses task-level recursion to revise an agent's harness without ground-truth verifiers, then extracts experience from those revisions into a continual-improvement harness for future tasks. The reported evaluations cover previously unseen professional tasks.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 9 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Directly addresses open-world harness adaptation, recursive self-improvement and transfer of improvement experience to novel tasks.

paper_pages.title: EmbodiedCLBench: Evaluating Continual Learning for Self-Evolving Embodied Agents
paper_pages.summary: Introduces an embodied-simulation benchmark centered on compositional generalization to measure whether self-evolving agents accumulate experience and transfer it to new tasks.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source verifies the title under identifier 2610.13021 and reports the original submission date as 2026-10-09.
paper_pages.relevance: Provides discovery-adjacent evaluation for continual learning, transfer, and adaptation in open-ended embodied environments.

paper_pages.title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
paper_pages.summary: Presents MASS, an RSI loop where a shared model acts as task solver, workflow optimizer, and evaluator through multiple agent instances, then trains on selected team trajectories to internalize collective improvements.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source identifies the paper under identifier 2610.12176 and reports its original submission date as 2026-10-08.
paper_pages.relevance: Addresses self-supervision when research tasks lack objective verification and human evaluation may become the bottleneck.

paper_pages.title: Open-ended Scientific Discovery with Possibilistic Reasoning
paper_pages.summary: The paper formalizes abductive autonomous scientific discovery with possibility theory, allowing agents to generate and test hypotheses while acknowledging that better explanations may remain undiscovered. It introduces an abductive-utility objective and an anytime-valid frontier-search algorithm.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 8 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Provides a formal treatment of open-ended hypothesis search, evidence accumulation and statistical validity when the hypothesis space is incomplete.

paper_pages.title: Memento 3: Model-Based Recursive Self-Improvement through Reflective Rulebooks
paper_pages.summary: A frozen LLM continually builds an explicit world model as a revisable natural-language rulebook, compiles it into executable code, and admits updates only after semantic and replay-based verification.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The arXiv page says “Submitted on 8 Oct 2026”; submission history lists v1 at 2026-10-08 12:06:54 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: Strong intersection of world-model learning, open-world exploration, verified memory updates, and test-time recursive improvement.

paper_pages.title: Language Models as AI Research World Models
paper_pages.summary: Uses language models to predict the outcomes of proposed research interventions from more than 2,600 prior experiments. Research experience improved intervention ranking and reduced selection regret, including across environments.
paper_pages.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 8 October 2026 at 16:18:54 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: Directly addresses learned world models for experimental selection, allowing AutoResearch agents to choose promising trials under limited budgets.

paper_pages.title: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement
paper_pages.summary: Offers reusable training, inference, rollout, evaluation, and sandbox services for data, harness, and joint improvement. It introduces RSI-Index to compare how much of the remaining performance gap research agents close.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The arXiv page says “Submitted on 7 Oct 2026”; submission history lists v1 at 2026-10-07 16:05:15 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: Important infrastructure and evaluation work for reproducible self-improvement experiments under explicit budgets and permissions.

paper_pages.title: RSI-Forge: From Research Papers to Environments for Recursive Self-Improvement
paper_pages.summary: Uses construction, reproduction, and review agents to convert published papers into executable research environments with automated evaluators, producing 210 environments across 18 fields.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The arXiv page says “Submitted on 7 Oct 2026”; submission history lists v1 at 2026-10-07 04:27:21 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: Scales the creation of scientifically grounded training and evaluation environments for agents that improve through repeated research attempts.

paper_pages.title: Kernel Autoresearch for Open-Ended Model Discovery
paper_pages.summary: Kernaut lets coding agents invent kernel functions as programs while construction contracts guarantee mathematical validity. A quality-diversity archive and functional novelty screening retain distinct candidates whose inductive biases transfer to unseen optimization and enzyme-kinetics tasks.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 7 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: A strong example of open-ended model discovery combining executable agent generation, validity constraints, diversity search and transfer evaluation.

paper_pages.title: DrugTargetWorld: A Synthetic Biobank for Training and Benchmarking AI Scientists
paper_pages.summary: Procedurally generates synthetic biobanks with concealed but known causal structure, enabling end-to-end training and evaluation of AI scientists for causal drug-target discovery without exposing private participant data.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The arXiv page says “Submitted on 7 Oct 2026” and verifies the title under identifier 2610.09558.
paper_pages.relevance: A concrete scientific-discovery world with causal ground truth, suitable for measuring hypothesis formation and end-to-end discovery workflows.

paper_pages.title: Can AI Agents Make Open-Ended Scientific Discovery? Evidence from Station
paper_pages.summary: Station places multiple agents in an open-world scientific ecosystem and adds supervision plus periodic meta-reflection to sustain research when intermediate metrics are absent. Agents are evaluated by how many findings from withheld research papers they independently rediscover.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 6 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Direct evidence about discovery-agent environments, persistent exploration, multi-agent research and evaluation through independent rediscovery.

paper_pages.title: Fork-and-Flush: Escaping Idea Basins in Autoresearch Agents
paper_pages.summary: Studies why independent autoresearch runs settle into different local idea regions and proposes branching and selective context removal to encourage broader exploration beyond an agent’s current trajectory.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source verifies the title under identifier 2610.07447 and reports the original submission date as 2026-10-05.
paper_pages.relevance: Directly addresses exploration collapse and idea diversity in open-ended autonomous research.

paper_pages.title: Evolving in Thought Space: Training a Small Model at Test Time Unlocks Better Discoveries
paper_pages.summary: Guidance-TTT adapts a compact model at test time to suggest high-level strategy changes while a stronger frozen model implements complete executable solutions. This separates strategic learning from implementation and reduces the cost of discovery-time policy updates.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 5 Oct 2026”; it also notes a later v2 revision on 12 Oct 2026, so the original paper date is retained.
paper_pages.relevance: Directly concerns test-time discovery training, verifier-guided search and a practical division between evolving strategy and frozen execution.

paper_pages.title: From Scientific Observations to Mechanisms: Benchmarking Hypothesis Generation by AI Scientists
paper_pages.summary: Introduces MechHypoBench, which tests whether AI scientists can infer mechanisms from complex empirical observations across 14 fields and 17.98 million records. Generated hypotheses are evaluated through predictions under withheld conditions, revealing a substantial mechanism-recovery gap.
paper_pages.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 4 October 2026 at 13:10:47 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: A focused discovery evaluation for moving beyond correlations toward falsifiable mechanistic hypotheses.

paper_pages.title: CURIO: Curiosity-Driven Test-Time Learning for Open-Ended Discovery
paper_pages.summary: CURIO augments task-reward learning with prediction-error bonuses from an intrinsic world model, encouraging exploration beyond the policy's most likely outputs. It reports gains on mathematical-discovery tasks and single-cell denoising together with increased program diversity.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 4 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Combines open-ended exploration, learned world-model signals and test-time reinforcement learning for scientific discovery.

paper_pages.title: Are We Measuring Scientific Intelligence? Rethinking the Evaluation of AI Scientists
paper_pages.summary: Tests whether AI-scientist answers actually follow supplied evidence by withdrawing or reversing evidence in benchmark data. High ordinary accuracy fell sharply under an evidence-grounded metric, showing that prior knowledge and shortcuts can masquerade as scientific reasoning.
paper_pages.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 4 October 2026 at 03:50:36 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: Provides a concrete discovery-evaluation protocol for separating evidence-grounded inference from recall or answer-key exploitation.

paper_pages.title: When Is Enough Enough in Self-Evolving LLM Systems?
paper_pages.summary: Develops an anytime-valid detector for deciding when iterative self-evolution should stop and a change-point method for selecting an earlier artifact when late updates overfit. Reported experiments substantially reduce compute while preserving unseen-test performance.
paper_pages.date_evidence: arXiv source page submission history identifies the initial October 3, 2026 version; candidate metadata agrees.
paper_pages.relevance: Supplies principled stopping and checkpoint-selection machinery for bounded recursive self-improvement.

paper_pages.title: EvoCast: Reliable Autonomous Research Agents for Iterative Forecasting Architecture Evolution
paper_pages.summary: Presents an autonomous forecasting-research system that diagnoses baselines, proposes evidence-grounded architecture changes, executes them, and accumulates results. Deterministic authorities constrain edits, evaluation, and promotion while agents retain open-ended hypothesis generation.
paper_pages.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 3 October 2026 at 13:30:53 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: A strong example of controlled AutoResearch combining open-ended exploration with reproducible experimental governance.

paper_pages.title: EvalResearchBench: Can AI Agents Build Their Own Feedback for Recursive Self-Improvement?
paper_pages.summary: Benchmarks agents that design executable evaluators by selecting tasks, implementing graders, and repairing them through pilots. The best agent-built evaluators approximate target-benchmark rankings but still suffer failures such as truncation and budget exhaustion.
paper_pages.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 3 October 2026 at 00:49:27 UTC; v2 followed on 16 October.
paper_pages.relevance: Directly studies whether recursive-improvement agents can construct the feedback signals needed to guide their own progress.

paper_pages.title: VERSE: Verified Self-Evolving Optimizer for Agent Harnesses
paper_pages.summary: Allows an optimizer to revise both an executor's harness and its own prompts, skills, tools, hooks, and notes while keeping model weights frozen. Execution-based verification, replay, and regression tracking produced held-out and out-of-distribution gains.
paper_pages.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 2 October 2026 at 00:16:30 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: A central agent-harness and recursive-self-improvement result demonstrating that verified optimizer self-modification can outperform fixed optimization workflows.

paper_pages.title: YouRA: A Persistent-State Architecture for Evidence-Traceable Autonomous Research Agents
paper_pages.summary: Introduces persistent state for hypotheses, gates, evidence pointers, failures, and recovery decisions across long research trajectories. Its separated controller and structured reflection improve end-to-end research scores and provenance diagnostics.
paper_pages.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 1 October 2026 at 05:40:21 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: Addresses evidence traceability, recovery, and durable research state—core infrastructure for reliable discovery agents.

paper_pages.title: Scientific Discovery under Validation Congestion via Multi-Fidelity Pairwise Rankings
paper_pages.summary: PRISMS prioritizes candidate molecules, materials and other designs using pairwise expert preferences instead of data-hungry absolute-score regressors. It selectively escalates uncertain comparisons to more expensive experts using a Fisher-information criterion.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 1 Oct 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Addresses experimental bottlenecks and budget-aware candidate selection using multiple evaluator fidelities, directly supporting scientific experimental design.

paper_pages.title: Can AI Scientists Coordinate at Runtime?
paper_pages.summary: Studies runtime selection and coordination among agents drawn from existing AI-scientist systems. Runtime agent selection improved observed mean scores, while extra contracts and verification had mixed effects under constrained budgets.
paper_pages.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 1 October 2026 at 03:18:07 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: Tests adaptive research-team orchestration rather than fixed, design-time scientific workflows.

paper_pages.title: SimEX: Simulation-Integrated Robotics AutoResearch
paper_pages.summary: Combines open-ended simulation experiments with a small number of physical trials to build and repair reusable robot tools. The reported system acquired manipulation skills without demonstrations and with ten minutes of real-robot interaction.
paper_pages.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 30 September 2026 at 04:58:21 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: Extends AutoResearch into embodied discovery, using simulation as an experimental laboratory and real trials as targeted corrective evidence.

paper_pages.title: Experimental Experience Modeling for Autonomous Research
paper_pages.summary: Builds a continually growing library of decision-relevant experimental experience. An agent retrieves prior evidence and runs a low-cost pilot only when that evidence is insufficient before committing to expensive full evaluation.
paper_pages.date_evidence: arXiv submission history: v1 submitted 30 September 2026 at 09:39:30 UTC.
paper_pages.relevance: Directly targets experimental design and efficient experiment selection for autonomous discovery agents.

paper_pages.title: Do Self-Evolving Skills Generalize to Held-Out Tasks?
paper_pages.summary: Evaluates whether repeatedly rewritten agent skills transfer beyond the tasks used to evolve them. It focuses on the gap between training-task improvement and genuine held-out generalization across several self-evolving skill methods.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source is record 2609.39148; its original-version metadata gives 30 September 2026.

paper_pages.summary: Shows that scalar feedback can hide tradeoffs among competing model behaviors. ConflictGuide exposes behavior-level conflicts so an AutoResearch loop can pursue edits that resolve them rather than merely improving a single aggregate score.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source is record 2609.39933; its original-version metadata gives 30 September 2026.

paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source is record 2609.36726; its original-version metadata gives 29 September 2026.

paper_pages.summary: Organizes large-scale biomedical resources around causal mechanisms and links them to a multi-million-edge evidence network. The proposed foundation is designed to evolve as additional population evidence becomes available.

paper_pages.summary: COEVOLVE runs multiple principle-evolution branches in parallel and transfers measurements through a coordination layer. Value-of-information routing and context-sensitive evidence weighting are intended to expand exploration while limiting harmful cross-branch transfer.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv source page explicitly states “Submitted on 28 Sep 2026.”
paper_pages.relevance: Explores multi-agent scientific discovery, evidence sharing, parallel hypothesis search and continual evolution of discovery principles.

paper_pages.title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
paper_pages.summary: Runs an AI research agent through repeated scaffold-improvement cycles under fixed budgets and hidden evaluations, with selected modifications transferring to held-out research tasks and domains.
paper_pages.date_evidence: The opened arXiv record reports the original submission on 2026-09-22 at 14:12:13 UTC.
